The Vault v0.6.7 stops Graphify from rebuilding project graphs over and over when nothing has changed.

## Graphify no longer rebuilds on file reads

- **Root cause.** On Windows, reading a file whose last-access time is more than about an hour old updates that time, and the file watcher reports it as a change. The desktop app treated every such read as a source edit, so agent sessions, editors, `git`, Vault reading its own memory files, and the builds themselves (which read every source file) kept queueing full rebuilds. One installation logged 311 builds across 31 projects in about a day, including more than three hours of builds for a single project.
- **Fix.** A change event now queues a build only when the file was written after the last build started. Creating, deleting or renaming files still queues a build as before.
- **Consistent exclusions.** The watcher now ignores exactly what the build ignores, including the built-in list and the project's `.graphifyignore`, instead of a shorter list of its own.

## Source app for Claude desktop sessions

- Claude desktop Code-tab sessions connect to MCP servers as `local-agent-mode-<server>`, so v0.6.6 still recorded their saves as `other`. They are now recorded as `claude`.

## Verification

- Full automated suite: 58 test files, 418 tests.
- Core, CLI, MCP server, and desktop type checks pass.
- End-to-end watcher check: read-only access to files with old access times produced watcher events but queued no builds; a real edit queued a build.

This build packages the desktop app and the bundled `vault-memory` MCP sidecar runtime. After installing, open The Vault and use Settings -> Client setup to connect Codex, Claude Desktop, or Claude Code.
